issue.title: Unify approval-time plan publication behind a single writer
issue.description:
After plan_archive_publication_recovery, the two approval-time publishers still write the same canonical plan path into sase--plans with different commit messages:

- src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_plan_accept.py commits "Add SDD files for <plan>" with push_after_commit=True
- sase._plan_archive_approval.archive_approved_plan commits "Archive approved plan <plan>" with a verified synchronous push

They now converge on create_time (archive reuses an existing destination stamp), so they no longer add/add-conflict on rebase. The redundant second write remains: every approval still produces two commits for one plan, two messages, and two publication paths that must stay byte-identical forever.

Scope: pick one publisher, delete or no-op the other for the canonical 202608/<plan>.md write, and keep a single commit message / push policy. Do not redo the reset-and-replay recovery work.

Out of scope of this task: migrating the SDD publication stack into sase-core.

Evidence: plan_archive_publication_recovery.md root-cause §1 and out-of-scope "The dual-writer design itself." Related (not a duplicate): sase-kb tracks repo-open add/add conflicts on "Add SDD files for …" commits; that is the same dual-writer collision class, but its remediation is sidecar refresh recovery rather than unifying the publishers.
